articles.headline: Malik Willis sparks Dolphins' first win, holding off a late Jets rally 28-25
articles.description: — Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score, leading the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: マリック・ウィリスがドルフィンズの初勝利を牽引、ジェッツの終盤の猛追を退け28-25で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: マリック・ウィリスが2本のタッチダウンパスと1本のランによる得点を挙げ、日曜日のニューヨーク・ジェッツ戦を28-25で制して、マイアミ・ドルフィンズに今季初勝利をもたらした。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score, leading the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday.


              The Dolphins (1-5) came off their bye-week break and avoided their first 0-6 start since 2019 by scoring on their first two drives and controlling most of the game before holding on to give coach Jeff Hafley his first win. 


              Trailing 28-17 with 4:44 left, the Jets (2-5) made a late push. On fourth-and-4, Geno Smith completed a short pass to Isaiah Davis, who zipped downfield 41 yards to the Dolphins 18. Three plays later, Smith found Mason Taylor in the back left corner of the end zone for a 12-yard touchdown, the tight end's second of the game. 


              Penalties negated New York's first two 2-point tries before Smith threw to Taylor to make it 28-25 with 3:24 left.


              But Willis sealed the victory when he pushed forward for 2 yards on fourth-and-1 as the Dolphins celebrated and frustrated Jets fans filed out of MetLife Stadium. 


              Willis was 14 of 21 for 208 yards and two TD passes to rookie Caleb Douglas, and ran for 37 yards on eight carries. Ollie Gordon rushed for 103 yards and a score. 


              Smith was 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three touchdowns, the two to Taylor and another to Omar Cooper Jr., and an interception. Braelon Allen had 104 yards rushing for the Jets, who dropped to 0-8 against AFC East opponents under Aaron Glenn.


              Dolphins and Jets start things off with a scoring spree
              The Dolphins started quickly, marching 76 yards on seven plays and taking their first lead in any game this season on Willis' 7-yard touchdown pass to Douglas.


              It also ended New York's streak of not allowing any points on an opening possession in five straight games.


              But the Jets came right back as Smith connected with Cooper for a 52-yard gain on their first offensive snap. Three plays later, Taylor — son of former Dolphins star and Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor — reached over Jason Marshall Jr. in the back of the end zone for a 13-yard score that tied it at 7.


              It's the third straight game in which New York scored on its opening drive.


              Miami then went on a 14-play, 60-yard run that was capped by Gordon's 1-yard touchdown run.


              New York was driving again on its next possession at the Miami 21 when Smith tried to fit a pass through a tight window to Taylor, but Michael Taaffe stepped in front and intercepted it.


              The Dolphins' touchdown streak ended on their third possession, though, when they went three-and-out. They got right back at it on their next drive, with Willis scoring on a 2-yard scramble with 6 seconds left in the first half to take a 21-7 lead.

Oct. 23:  Caleb Williams shows he is all the way back on TNF

By Adam Rank

There is going to be a lively debate between Chicago Bears and New England Patriots fans over the next number of years as to who got the better QB in the 2024 NFL draft. And, I hate to go all youth sports dad on you, but I'm just happy that both players are doing well.

And you should, too. Caleb Williams not only entered the NFL MVP conversation Thursday night, but he's a rock-solid starter for your fantasy team moving forward as well. This Bears offense has been on fire with Williams under center. The Bears have scored 120 points in the three games he has started and finished. He is just the third quarterback in Bears history with 300-plus passing yards and a win in back-to-back games, joining Billy Wade (1962) and Sid Luckman (1947). You can forgive Bears supporters for being a little excited about Caleb.

• You might remember when people were taunting Williams for being a checkdown merchant. Well, he had eight completions of 20-plus yards against the Patriots. That is tied for the most by a quarterback in a game this season.

• Luther Burden III has 250 yards after the catch this season, the second-highest total in the league behind Drake London (255). Burden finished the game with four receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. He wasn't the target leader, but Burden is the top wide receiver to trust for the Bears moving forward.

• Rome Odunze was clutch down the stretch for the Bears. Two big grabs on the final drive to set up the field goal that made it a two-score game. He also corralled the onside kick to seal the win. Great for the Bears. I'm not sure he's going to be somebody you can rely on week to week in fantasy. He's good for bye-week and injury replacement, but don't rush him into your lineups.

articles.headline: Michael Penix Jr. throws 3 TD passes, Falcons force 4 turnovers to give 49ers first loss, 29-20
articles.description: — Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20 on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・ペニックス・ジュニアが3本のTDパス、ファルコンズが4つのターンオーバーを誘い49ersに今季初敗戦を喫させる 29-20
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・ペニックス・ジュニアが3つのタッチダウンパスを投げ、アトランタは4つのターンオーバーから13得点を奪った。ファルコンズは日曜日の試合で、サンフランシスコ・49ersに29-20で今季初敗戦を突きつけた。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- — Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20 on Sunday.


              San Francisco (6-1) was already thin at wide receiver before its offense faced additional limitations when running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury. 


              Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels intercepted Brock Purdy's pass intended for Jordan Watkins with 2:34 remaining. It was Purdy's second interception. Daniels then recovered a fumble by George Kittle with less than a minute remaining.


              The 49ers had only six turnovers in their first six games.


              Penix threw scoring passes to tight ends Nick Muse and Kyle Pitts before giving Atlanta (3-4) a 26-14 lead with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Drake London in the fourth quarter. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with no interceptions.


              The 49ers' comeback attempt was hurt when a lengthy review by the officials took away Purdy's apparent 23-yard touchdown pass to Watkins. Following the ruling, Purdy was sacked on fourth down by Za'Darius Smith.


              Purdy's 1-yard scoring pass to fullback Kyle Juszcyk with 5:05 remaining cut Atlanta's lead to 26-20 before Eddy Pineiro extra-point attempt was wide left — his fourth miss of the season.


              A shanked punt by Atlanta's Jake Bailey allowed San Francisco to start a possession at its 47 with about four minutes remaining. The 49ers wasted the excellent field position and opportunity to mount a go-ahead drive when Purdy threw his second interception that led to Nick Folk's 31-yard field goal.


              Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and the two picks.


              Bijan Robinson rushed for 63 yards as the Falcons snapped a two-game skid. McCaffrey was limited to seven carries for 39 yards.


              McCaffrey's backup, Kaelon Black, lost a fumble at the Atlanta 29 that was recovered by Gervon Dexter Sr. in the second quarter. A long Atlanta drive set up Nick Folk's 33-yard field goal.


              In the third quarter, Jessie Bates III intercepted Purdy's pass at the Atlanta 10 to set up the touchdown drive capped by the scoring pass to London.


              The 49ers leaned heavily on McCaffrey on their opening touchdown drive. McCaffrey had two catches for 40 yards, including a 24-yard gain to the Atlanta 5. He had four carries for 29 yards, including a scoring fourth-down leap over the pile from the 1.


              McCaffrey had a 5-yard catch on the 49ers' next drive before leaving the game with the thigh injury. He was listed as questionable to return as he was examined in the injury tent. McCaffrey emerged, put on his helmet and tested the thigh by running on the sideline before heading to the locker room.

articles.headline: Vikings defense clamps down on Daniel Jones and the Colts for a 16-10 victory to stay undefeated
articles.description: — Harrison Smith capped another dominant performance by Minnesota's defense with the game-sealing interception, and the Vikings overcame another sluggish start to stay unbeaten with a 16-10...
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスの守備陣がダニエル・ジョーンズとコルツを封じ込め、16-10で勝利し無敗を維持
articles.descriptionJa: ハリソン・スミスが試合を決定づけるインターセプトを決め、ミネソタのディフェンスによるまたしても圧倒的なパフォーマンスを締めくくった。バイキングスは再び立ち上がりの遅さを克服し、16-10で勝利して無敗を維持した...
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Harrison Smith capped another dominant performance by Minnesota's defense with the game-sealing interception, and the Vikings overcame another sluggish start to stay unbeaten with a 16-10 victory over the spiraling Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.


              Linebacker Blake Cashman led the onslaught of pressure on Daniel Jones all afternoon with 12 tackles, two sacks, four passes defensed and three quarterback hits for the Vikings (6-0), who won yet again despite minimal production from Kyler Murray and the offense.


              Smith picked off Jones around midfield with about a minute left to kill the last-ditch drive by the Colts (2-5) before it ever got going, the 40th career interception for the stalwart safety who decided right before the regular season to return for his 15th year.


              Jones went 13 for 122 for 108 yards and lost 44 yards on four sacks, with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores continually sending blitzers into the backfield.


              Will Reichard made three field goals for the Vikings, including a 52-yarder with 1:39 left after his 59-yard try was blocked by Grover Stewart earlier in the fourth quarter.


              Jonathan Taylor gave the Colts the lead they kept for more than three quarters of the game with a 38-yard touchdown run on their opening drive, but Spencer Shrader missed two field goals in the second half.


              The miss from 56 yards that coach Shane Steichen called for on fourth-and-2 set the Vikings up for their only touchdown, when Murray used a 35-yard run to get in range for a short scoring pass to T.J. Hockenson.


              Two of the NFL's best kickers are automatic no more
              Reichard hit from 28 and 47 yards in the second quarter to set the franchise record with 35 consecutive made field goals, which was the longest active streak in the league — until the block.


              Shrader, who leads the NFL in scoring this season with 70 points, had his streak of 22 straight made field goals end with his wide-left miss that had heavy pressure off the edge by former Colts cornerback Isaiah Rodgers. That also stopped Shrader's run of seven makes in a row from 50-plus yards.


              Injury report
              Colts: With standout Sauce Gardner (calf) inactive, the CB depth chart was chewed up in the second half when Justin Walley (knee) and Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) left with injuries. ... TE Tyler Warren (groin) missed his second straight game. LB Jaylon Carlies (ribs) returned to the starting lineup after missing two games.


              Vikings: RB Aaron Jones aggravated a nagging knee injury in the fourth quarter when he took a low hit at the end of a 17-yard run. He didn't return. ... Myles Price, who returned the opening kickoff 46 yards and leads the league in punt return average, was evaluated for a concussion in the first quarter but did not miss any time.

articles.headline: Sixers overrule Embiid, sit center with plantar fasciitis management
articles.description: Despite publicly calling to play Sunday against the Pistons, the 76ers decided to sit Joel Embiid due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
articles.headlineJa: シックスターズ、エンビードの意向を覆し、足底筋膜炎のケアのためセンターを欠場させる
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のピストンズ戦への出場を公言していたものの、76ersは右足の足底筋膜炎のケアのため、ジョエル・エンビードを欠場させることを決定した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- A day after Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid asked reporters to campaign for him to play in Sunday's game against Detroit -- the second of the Sixers' first back-to-back this season -- the 76ers ruled out Embiid for Sunday night's game against the Detroit Pistons with right foot plantar fasciitis management. ​

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said with a smile after Saturday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

 

The Sixers decided against Embiid's wishes, as they look to keep the former MVP healthy for a long season. Embiid, plagued by various injuries, has averaged just 49 games per season over his 10 years.

In their win over the Bucks on Saturday, Embiid had his tenth career triple-double, finishing with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Having him sidelined is a significant blow to the Sixers' already thin frontcourt.

Philadelphia also ruled out big men Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad). Walker injured his left knee in Saturday's win, exiting the game in the third quarter. That leaves Adem Bona as the team's only true center active on Sunday. Forward Dean Wade, who made his season debut on Saturday, will likely play some center, and LeBron James, who missed Saturday's game with sciatica management, has no injury designation and can also help out at the center spot.

The Pistons will be without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who the team said has a hamstring injury and will be out for at least two weeks.

articles.headline: McKennie scores 1st goal since April in much-needed Juventus win
articles.description: Weston McKennie opened the scoring for Juventus in a 2-0 win over Lecce on Sunday to help the Serie A side course correct after a pair of disappointing results.
articles.headlineJa: マッケニーが4月以来のゴールを決め、ユヴェントスが待望の勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ウェストン・マッケニーが日曜日のレッチェ戦で先制点を挙げ、ユヴェントスは2-0で勝利。2試合連続の不振に喘いでいたセリエAのチームにとって、軌道修正につながる重要な勝利となった。
articles.body:
Weston McKennie opened the scoring for Juventus in a 2-0 win over Lecce on Sunday to help the Serie A side course correct after a pair of disappointing results.

The United States midfielder swooped in to redirect a free kick over the top of the Lecce defense into the back of the net just before the 30-minute mark. It was his first goal in Serie A this season and first in all competitions for Juventus since April -- ending a 13-game drought.

Douglas Luiz scored another for the visitors just before halftime to Luciano Spalletti's side all it would need to pick up the three points and move up to seventh in the table on 14 points.

Juventus had lost their last game in Serie A -- a lackluster draw against Lazio last weekend -- before having to come from behind to draw with Stade Rennais 2-2 in the Europa League on Thursday.

Boos could be heard ringing down on Spalletti and his team after the draw with Rennes at the Allianz in Turin in midweek as the former Italy manager looks to get Juventus back on course in Serie A and in Europe.

McKennie was left out of the U.S. squad in the September/October international window in which Mauricio Pochettino brought in a number of new faces in the team's first games since losing to Belgium in the round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup last summer.

Information from ESPN Global Research was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Luis Enrique: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will be back stronger for PSG after ACL injury
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique says winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will come back stronger after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury.
articles.headlineJa: ルイス・エンリケ監督「クヴァラツヘリアはACL負傷から、より強くなってPSGに戻ってくる」
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのルイス・エンリケ監督は、前十字靭帯（ACL）を負傷したウィングのフイチア・クヴァラツヘリアが、より強くなって復帰すると語った。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique says winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will come back stronger after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

The 25-year-old suffered the injury during PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona and is now ruled out for the remainder of the season.

Kvaratskhelia has been a key player for PSG over the last few years, having helped the club to back-to-back Champions League titles, and will be a big miss for Les Parisiens going forward.

Enrique says the Georgia international will continue to be an important player for the club once he has recovered from the injury.

He said: "Unfortunately, we already suspected after the game how serious the injury was. Our thoughts are with the player and what he's going to go through, it's difficult.

"But ultimately, you have to stay positive and remember that if you want to play at the highest level for 10 to 15 years, you're going to suffer injuries, that's the life of a professional footballer.

"Kvara is a fighter, you have to try and look for the positives, and there will be some, once he's overcome this injury. He has been, is and will continue to be a very important player for us. We'll stand by him and be attentive to his needs. He'll come back even stronger, I have no doubt about that.

"No injury means that we absolutely must sign a new player. Since the start of the season, I've always said that we could cope with any injuries."

PSG will welcome Lyon to Parc des Princes on Monday as they look for a fifth straight win, hoping to climb further up the table.

PSG were beaten 2-1 by Lyon in April in the last meeting between the two sides and Enrique says the result has given him extra motivation.

- PSG-Lyon match moved to Monday amid Paris protests, NFL game

- PSG star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptures ACL; Dembélé, Marquinhos out 'weeks'

- Cristiano Ronaldo leads Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tributes after ACL injury

He added: "It's a motivation to take on Paulo Fonseca's Olympique Lyonnais. We remember what they did last season, when they won at the Parc des Princes playing very well.

"It's up to us to show that we're ready for every game and to demonstrate our form. It's an extra motivation to play against this Olympique Lyonnais side.

"We've shown we can improve our results in the league. Three or four weeks ago, we were still a long way behind the top team in the table. And now, we have the chance to go top. It's important for us to be as high up the table as possible."

articles.headline: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois out of Clasico with flu
articles.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのGKティボ・クルトワ、インフルエンザのためクラシコを欠場
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードのゴールキーパー、ティボ・クルトワは、インフルエンザによりバルセロナとのクラシコを欠場する。
articles.body:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu.

Courtois, 34, is a key player for Madrid, but is absent for the LaLiga match at Camp Nou, which kicks off with Madrid trailing leaders Barça by six points in the table.

He is replaced in goal by Andriy Lunin, 27, who has been a regular deputy for Courtois in recent seasons, including in Madrid's run to the Champions League final in 2024.

"Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight's LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu," the club said in a brief statement before confirming his absence in their team announcement. "Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place."

Madrid go into the Clásico under pressure, having already lost twice in LaLiga this season -- at Real Betis and Atletico Madrid -- while Barcelona have won all of their league games.

However, Madrid's form has improved since the international break, with Courtois playing a starring role, including in their 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig in midweek.

The visitors will also be without Vinícius Júnior at Camp Nou, as he continues his four-game domestic ban.

articles.headline: Man United are stuck with their underperforming players no matter who's manager
articles.description: Man United can dismiss Michael Carrick, but whoever replaces him will face the same problems: a squad that continues to fail the club and its fans.
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Michael Carrick couldn't get a reaction out of these Manchester United players when he needed one most. If the same thing happens to the next manager, one of the biggest clubs in Europe will be facing the prospect of relegation from the Premier League.

Fresh off the back of the humiliating 4-1 defeat to Como in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, Carrick spent the first five minutes of his news conference on Friday pleading with his squad to show that they cared enough to put in a completely different performance.

In his desperation for a change of fortunes, he dropped Bruno Fernandes following the captain's incendiary comments about the game plan in Italy. But with his job on the line, Carrick got another shambolic display as AFC Bournemouth won 3-0 at Old Trafford to leave United 16th in the Premier League table and just one point above the drop zone.

With the 45-year-old now on the brink of the sack, good luck to whoever takes over.

At one point, the Bournemouth fans began to sing "you're going down with the City." Manchester City are still waiting for their punishment after being found guilty of breaking financial rules, and United have just one league win all season. It's not as unthinkable as it sounds.

Forget qualifying for the Champions League. United's immediate worry is getting sucked into a battle for survival. Either way, it's unlikely that Carrick will be around to see it.

Asked directly after the game whether he expected to be dismissed, the former United midfielder admitted he was in the dark.

"I totally understand the situation," he said. "I am not expecting anything, I'm carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always carry on doing what I think is the best for the football club."

After another game that summed up United's perilous position, it will be a surprise if Carrick survives long enough to walk out against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in six days' time. Another defeat there and United could be in the bottom three.

They are a team completely devoid of any confidence and buckling under the pressure of the intense Old Trafford spotlight. There were nerves and anxiety on show from the very beginning against Bournemouth, just as there was against Como.

Ayden Heaven needlessly gave the ball away and then charged into a two-footed lunge to gift Bournemouth a free kick. Rayan was left completely unmarked at the back post to tap in.

Next it was Leny Yoro's turn to produce a catastrophic mistake. After dithering on the ball, the once-capped France international slipped and let Adrien Truffert make a simple pass for Marcus Tavernier to score.

The less said about Bournemouth's third -- Senne Lammens caught in no-man's land after rushing out to hopeful ball forward and Evanilson shooting into an empty net -- the better.

Three basic errors and three goals conceded. Their three league games against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool look incredibly daunting.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich hold off Freiburg in first game without Kompany
articles.description: Bayern Munich returned to the top of the Bundesliga table thanks to a 3-1 away win at Freiburg on Sunday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich returned to the top of the Bundesliga table thanks to a 3-1 away win at Freiburg on Sunday.

It was the champions' first game since manager Vincent Kompany was admitted to hospital after collapsing at the club's training ground, with assistant Aaron Danks in the dugout in his absence.

A victory for Borussia Dortmund against Frankfurt on Saturday had knocked Bayern off the summit, but goals from Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry in the first half earned them victory in what turned into a tricky assignment.

Midfielder Tom Bischof's own-goal eight minutes from the end set up a nervous finish at the Europa-Park Stadion, before Michael Olise scored in the fifth minute of stoppage time to put the result beyond doubt.

Kompany's absence is expected to be weeks rather than days, according to the club's director of sport Max Eberl.

The former Manchester City and Belgium defender Kompany remained in a stable condition in hospital and on Friday, and Eberl said "examinations were continuing."

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday

A seven-game Sunday slate features a series of potential competitive contests. Only one game on the docket claims a double-digit point spread -- a departure from a Saturday field that was full of large lines. The marquee matchup of the day features the Minnesota Timberwolves hosting the Toronto Raptors in a meeting of deep, darkhorse contenders.

Close games bode well for developing fantasy and betting angles, as rotations and workloads prove more predictable in competitive games. A good place to start during a busy day of basketball is the injury report, which tells us that we won't see Paolo Banchero, Zach Edey or Jalen Duren playing for their respective teams. Joel Embiid, meanwhile, is set to rest for the second leg of a back-to-back series for the Philadelphia 76ers.

While we're still learning how each rotation and coaching staff will react to the absence of big names from the gameplan, we can proactively make some decisions based on precedent and prediction. 

For the Orlando Magic, a proven veteran big man is due for more minutes and work in the wake of Banchero's ankle injury, as you'll read below. What will Memphis do sans Edey? How will Detroit cope with being sans their interior anchor in South Philly tonight? 

And, those 76ers don't have a one-to-one backup for Embiid like they did in seasons past in the form of Andre Drummond. They will instead likely turn to a collective and small-ball looks -- possible even some featuring LeBron at center. We'll learn a lot today about all of these sides, which can serve us in future slates, as well.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

 Wendell Carter Jr., C, Orlando Magic (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)

With Banchero in street clothes for tonight's tilt with the New York Knicks, Carter should see more minutes, rebounding chances, and post touches as a result. The Knicks lack the interior defense and rebounding from last season's run, supporting confidence in double-double upside for this veteran big.

Paul Reed, C/PF, Detroit Pistons (14.2%)

Assuming Philadelphia decides to rest Embiid in the second game of a back-to-back, they will likely turn to a number of different looks to cover for him. Reed, who will consume a good bit of the work reserved for Duren, would then be facing a 76ers lineup badly lack rebounding acumen, establishing a nice floor for this active and unique frontcourt talent. Indiana Pacers (1-1, ninth in the Eastern Conference) vs. Brooklyn Nets (0-2, 13th in the Eastern Conference)


              New York; Sunday, 6 p.m. EDT


              LINE: Pacers -7.5; over/under is 231.5


              BOTTOM LINE: Brooklyn plays Indiana in a matchup of Eastern Conference teams.


              Brooklyn finished 20-62 overall and 14-37 in Eastern Conference play a season ago. The Nets averaged 105.9 points per game while allowing opponents to score 115.9 last season.


              Indiana went 19-63 overall and 15-37 in Eastern Conference play during the 2025-26 season. The Pacers allowed opponents to score 120.4 points per game and shoot 48.9% from the field last season.


              INJURIES: Nets: Tyler Bilodeau: out (shoulder).
